title: autopilot ledger removal L1: PR events are decided by the event log and reviewer re-checks by a per-head record, with no once() ledger entry
acceptance: Why. Two more action classes still run through the `once()` write-ahead ledger (`once` at bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:210-223, `recover` at :225-230): PR events (`observe_pr`, bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:67-78, `self.once(['pr-event', number, kind], ...)` at :76) and reviewer re-check requests (`recheck`, bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:334-350, `self.once(['recheck', number, head, name], ...)` at :350). In both, one failed command parks the action as 'uncertain' forever and queues 'Mechanical action needs reconciliation', and the action is never tried again. For PR events that is a correctness problem since T-193: `landed()` (bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:39-55) reads the `merged` event row, so a lost `merged` row lets a merged PR be gated again. This task is step L1 of the reviewed plan state/briefs/PLAN-2026-10-05-remaining-issues.md (item 4): `pr-event` and `recheck` leave the ledger. `restack` and `launch-review` stay as they are; later steps take them. T-190 (update) and T-193 (advance) are the patterns this task follows.

Existing tests that pin the old behaviour change in place, and no others:
- tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py `test_terminal_and_open_events_are_once_and_keep_task_grammar` (about 168-182) calls `observe_pr` twice with an `emit` stub that writes nothing, so today only `once()` stops the second emit. Make its emit stub append the row to `self.state / 'events.jsonl'` the way fm-emit.sh does (`type`, `task`, `pr`, `actor`), then keep its assertions (one emit per state, task grammar, actor 'github').
- tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py `test_team_merge_is_observed_once_without_invoking_merge` (259-273) calls `closed_pull` twice for the same merged PR and asserts one call. Its setUp `emit` stub (tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py:46) records only, and outside a poll `rows()` reads events.jsonl, so today only `once()` stops the second emit. Give it (or setUp, if no other test depends on the stub writing nothing) an emit stub that also appends the row to `self.state / 'events.jsonl'` like fm-emit.sh; keep its assertions.
- tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py `test_task_lookup_and_observation_do_not_use_operation_channel` (about 150-165) calls `observe_pr` with `command` failing on use; it keeps passing, because `emit` is stubbed there and `observe_pr` adds no `command` call.
- tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py `test_recheck_respects_local_projection` (243-252): rewritten as described above.
- tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py:361 and tests/lib/merge_authorization.py:157 replace `observe_pr` with a no-op and need no change.
No other test depends on the ledger stopping a repeat event or re-check: besides these, check every caller of `closed_pull` (`grep -rn closed_pull tests/`) and of `recheck`; `grep -rn -e recheck -e pr-event -e observe_pr -e requested_reviewers tests/` lists only the tests above and unrelated uses (tests/external-reviews.test.sh, tests/onboarding-crew.test.sh, tests/herdr/credentials.py, tests/lib/spec_pins_cases.py use the words in other senses); confirm by reading them. Every `assertEqual(...data['actions'], {})` keeps passing.

Docs, edited in place in their home sections (T-189 rule; nothing appended at the end of design.md):
- design/design.md §15.8 'Pilot and advanced integration', the paragraph beginning 'Branch updates are re-decided from GitHub state' (about 5218-5236): say that PR events are decided by the event log alone (an event already in events.jsonl is never written again; a failed write retries at offsets 0, 1 and 3, then wakes once), that reviewer re-check requests are recorded per PR head in `rechecked` and completed when GitHub lists the reviewer as requested (201) or already requested, that a 422 refusal wakes once without retry, and that `migrated_t200` drops legacy pr-event, recheck and observed-merge actions with their undelivered wakes, marking a terminal PR whose pr-event action was not done as `event_pending` so its row is written by the normal retry series. Change the sentence 'The remaining write-ahead classes are re-check, restack, review launch and PR events …' to name only restack and review launch.
- docs/autopilot.md, the paragraph 'Branch update steps no longer write reconciliation records…' (about 50-62): the same facts in the same words, and the same change to 'The remaining write-ahead classes are …'.
- The module docstring of bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py (:1-6) stays.

Scope boundary. No change to `restack()` (bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:352-362), the `launch-review` call (bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:305), `once()` or `recover()` themselves (they still serve those two classes), jobs, `advance`, `sync_branch` or `update_branch`. No GitHub request is added for PR events. The only new GitHub call is the re-check POST, which replaces `command` with `probe` plus `--include` on the same endpoint.

In flight. Nothing in flight edits bin/lib/fm_autopilot*.py or design §15.8 (T-193 and T-195 have merged). The running autopilot keeps its old snapshot until it is replaced: `fm-autopilot.sh ensure` exits early while a service runs (bin/fm-autopilot.sh:52-55), so after this merges firstmate stops the service and runs `bin/fm-autopilot.sh ensure --all` (that gap is plan item 2, a separate task). `migrated_t200` runs at that start. Today's state holds 11 pr-event, 5 observed-merge and 2 launch-review actions, all 'done'; the first two classes are removed and launch-review stays. The five tasks queued after this one in the plan (T-196 CI coverage, cursor store, host/legacy receipts, worker notes, review carry) do not touch these files; the later restack and launch-review steps and the reload task touch fm_autopilot.py and must start after this merges.

Workers do not run the suites. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Fail-first is expected from `tests/autopilot.test.sh` (autopilot_cases.py), `tests/autopilot-loop.test.sh` (autopilot_loop.py) and `tests/sync-prs.test.sh` (autopilot_sync.py): the new event-retry, event_pending/no-restart, re-check retry/422/requested and migration tests are red on base and green on head. The in-poll dedup test, the 'row already present' test and the merge-authorization ready-list test are regression guards: green on base and head. tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py is 700 lines and autopilot_cases.py 565; each test module stays under 1200 lines. If new tests would push one past that, put them in a new module, tests/lib/autopilot_ledger_l1.py, run by a new tests/autopilot-ledger-l1.test.sh in the style of tests/autopilot-loop.test.sh. Every new test module that can reach a card sets `os.environ['HERDR_ENV'] = '0'` at top level, as tests/decide.test.sh:1024 requires. bin/ci.sh discovers tests/*.test.sh and balances shards by itself, so a new suite needs no edit there.
